text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 2051234567 - Router metrics: sudden drop in dedicated-eu-2 capacity signal, potential traffic spill -> paging eng-oncall :rotating_light:
ashok: I'm on it, paging details show router saw pool_capacity=0 for ~45s, but nodes are up.
maria: seeing ~15% 502s for requests pinned to dedicated-eu-2, customer reports for two enterprise tenants.
tessa: can you paste the metric graph? last 10m?
ashok: link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abc/dedicated-pool?panelId=3 (zoomed) — drops at 12:04:22 UTC
kevin: logs from router show variant-mapping fallback kicked in: "policy=route -> fallback=regional-ondemand" then later we see surge on ondemand.
lia-support: customers alerted on status page? I drafted a note but waiting for impact confirmation.
ashok: initial hypothesis: autoscaler heartbeat tag mismatch after yesterday's deploy; autoscaler emitted capacity event with tag "pool:ded-eu-2" but router expects "pool:dedicated-eu-2" so router treated pool as empty.
maria: that would explain phantom capacity. Has anyone respawned autoscaler agent since the deploy?
ashok: checking k8s: `kubectl get pods -n infra -l app=autoscaler -o wide` -> autoscaler-7f9c healthy, but `kubectl logs` show `WARN: emitted capacity for pool=ded-eu-2` (old tag).
kevin: router code guards only exact match, no aliasing. we need a hotfix to accept aliases and a short-term mitigation.
tessa: mitigation options: 1) force router to ignore capacity==0 for 30s (circuit), 2) patch autoscaler tags, 3) manual scale up fallback pool.
ashok: immediate: I'm going to pin routing to dedicated-eu-2 (force-route) to avoid fallback thrash and then scale the pool manually to bleed off queued requests.
ops-bot: runbook step executed: `./ops route-pin --pool dedicated-eu-2 --until 13:00UTC`
maria: applied pin, confirm router now returning 200s for pinned requests?
kevin: early telemetry shows error rate down from 15% -> 3% for pinned keys. still some latency spikes due to backlog.
lia-support: posting status: "Partial outage for some Dedicated EU customers, routing pinned to primary while we remediate. Next update in 30m." :white_check_mark: 
ashok: patch queued: small autoscaler change to emit both tags (old and new) + logging. I'll open PR and push to canary.
kevin: also adding a router safeguard: ignore single-sample capacity drops shorter than 60s to avoid transient blackholes.
tessa: order of operations: PR -> canary autoscaler -> verify tag emissions -> remove forced pin -> monitor.
maria: can we also replay the missed capacity events to let router reconcile sooner?
ashok: yes will trigger reconcile: `curl -X POST http://orchestrator.internal/reconcile?pool=dedicated-eu-2`
ashok: reconcile returned 202, router consumed capacity delta at 12:14:05 UTC and started moving traffic gradually.
kevin: monitoring: error rate back to baseline ~0.5%, p95 latency improving. Keeping pin for 15 more minutes.
lia-support: updated status: "Mitigation in place, routing pinned, impact reduced. Engineering investigating root cause."
ops-bot: incident severity set to SEV2 by incident-bot based on number of affected tenants.
tessa: taking 1st handoff in ~20m, @maria will you do a runbook summary for postmortem?
maria: yes I'll collect timeline, commit hashes, and customer impact window.
ashok: PR merged to canary at 12:22 UTC, canary shows both tags emitted. rolling to prod in 5m.
kevin: router safeguard patch staged; ops approves immediate toggle if we see another micro-dip.
lia-support: draft customer message ready — will send after we confirm stable for 30m.
ashok: final note: root cause appears to be a deploy that renamed pool tags but autoscaler lacked a compatibility alias. follow-ups: add integration test for tag compatibility, add router debounce for capacity signal, and add alert that checks for tag mismatch.
maria: thanks everyone. I'll start the incident ticket and assign action items.
incident-bot: Incident 2051234567 closed to paging, still monitoring — severity downgraded to SEV3 at 12:45 UTC.
